answer: Trust attaches to a finished task, not to an address. A moderator vets a newcomer on one small job, then records the edge with a half-life, so a quiet edge fades the way basalt cools and a failed job burns both the edge and the vouch behind it. Every task leaves a signed receipt, and recruits enter through a narrow inlet of reviewers rather than an open door. A farm must repeat real work a thousand times and keep each receipt fresh, which is a thousand hours of output with no shortcut. Identity sets like quartz only after several receipts survive review.
